newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals - Aluminium premiums up for 2nd qtr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals - Aluminium premiums up for 2nd qtr.

text.p: South Korean aluminium premiums for second quarter shipment were set at around $88 a tonne over London Metal Exchange's (LME) cash average prices in line with higher Japanese import premiums, traders said on Thursday.
This compared with $65-$70 a tonne over LME cash average prices basis CIF Pusan for first quarter shipment, they said.
"Aluminium import premiums are strong, mainly affected by higher premiums in Japan," a trader with Daewoo Corp said.
South Korean firms normally settle the premiums with reference to the average offical LME cash prices of the previous month, so April shipment would be based on March quotes.
On Wednesday, Japanese traders said aluminium import premiums for the second quarter were set at about $82 a tonne over LME cash prices, up $20 a tonne from the previous quarter.

The increase, which was widely expected, reflected a rise in Japan's spot premiums since the beginning of the year due to firmer U.S. Midwest premiums and strong demand from Japan's automobile and construction sectors, they said.
South Korean aluminium import premiums for spot delivery have remained unchanged at $90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices over the past week, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices rose to 1.5 million won a tonne delivered from 1.48 million won a week ago, while copper prices remained unchanged at 2.279 million won.
Zinc prices rose to 1.15 million won a tonne from 1.079 million won a week earlier in line with higher prices on the LME, while lead prices were unchanged at 728,000 won.

Zinc traders said local trading houses were holding physical supplies back from the market on expectations that Korea Zinc will raise its selling prices early next week due to recent price hikes on the LME.
"Local suppliers are holding physicals this week since they expect higher prices next week," a Samsung Corp trader said.
Korea Zinc, South Korea's largest zinc and lead producer, posts its domestic selling prices at the begining of each month, reflecting the previous month's LME monthly cash average prices.
Korea Zinc's selling prices is the benchmark for domestic physical trades.

Traders said South Korea imported 26,699 tonnes of special high grade zinc and 1,664 tonnes of high grade zinc from China in 1996. Last year, South Korea's zinc imports totalled 89,364 tonnes, excluding between 40,000 tonnes to 50,000 tonnes of North Korean zinc. They did not give the comparitive figures for the previous year.
